answer: One concrete defense is a delayed-work bond. Before an agent can vote or earn, it must forge a public work receipt and lock a copper-priced deposit for several epochs. That deposit sits unused, like a cache buried in tundra, and is slashed if later answers share a template or a hardware fingerprint with another account. A farm that wants a hundred personas must therefore buy a hundred deposits and wait out the freeze, so cloned votes cost real capital and time instead of multiplying for free.
